meta.name: Cursor Daily Driver
meta.description: A spoon-fed 21-day mastery path that turns Cursor into your daily driver for personal work, web activity, and automation — written for a non-technical layman.

workPlan.tagline: Make Cursor your personal operating system — without becoming a programmer
workPlan.audience: You: smart, busy, non-technical. You want AI to handle writing, research, organizing, web chores, and repeatable personal workflows — safely and confidently.
outcomes: Open Cursor first for almost any knowledge or computer task
Pick the right mode (Ask / Plan / Agent / Debug) without guessing
Write clear prompts using fill-in-the-blank Variables
Run ready-made Recipes for email, research, docs, trips, and file cleanup
Teach Cursor your preferences with User Rules and project rules
Connect tools via MCP and delegate longer jobs to Cloud Agents
Review AI work like a manager — not a spectator
method: Day = short lesson + flashcards + one Recipe practice + quiz
Mastery Visas stamp real competence (pass quizzes, not vibes)
Week 2: context, rules, recipes for personal work & web
Week 3: skills, MCP, Cloud Agents, daily-driver OS, capstone
Keep a 'Wins' folder of prompts that worked
rulesOfEngagement: Speak like a boss giving a clear brief — not like you're coding
Never paste passwords, bank logins, or secrets into chat
Always read the summary of what Cursor changed before you Accept
If confused, switch to Ask mode and say: 'Explain like I'm not technical'
Missed a day? Do 10 flashcards only — no guilt stacking
Pass score is 80% (85% on Capstone Mastery)

modules.title: What Cursor Actually Is
modules.subtitle: A plain-English mental model for non-tech humans

sections.heading: Forget 'code editor' for a minute
sections.body: Cursor looks like a writing app for computer files. Under the hood it is a super-capable assistant that can read your folders, draft text, reorganize files, run careful computer steps, and explain what it is doing in English. You do not need to become a programmer to benefit. You need to become a clear manager of an eager helper.

sections.heading: The boss / assistant metaphor
sections.body: You are the boss. Cursor is the assistant. Good bosses give clear goals, point at the right documents, set limits ('do not delete anything'), and review the work. Bad bosses say 'fix my life' and get surprised. This whole course trains you to be a great boss of AI.

sections.heading: What Cursor is great at (for you)
sections.body: Drafting emails and documents; summarizing long notes; turning messy thoughts into checklists; researching topics and citing sources; renaming/sorting files with your approval; building simple personal tools (trackers, templates); and repeating workflows you teach it once.

sections.heading: What you still own
sections.body: Judgment, truth-checking, private data, money decisions, and final sends. Cursor can draft the email; you decide whether to hit send. That partnership is the daily driver.

keyTakeaways: Cursor = powerful assistant for files + tasks, not a magic mind-reader
Your job is clear briefs + review
No coding degree required — clear English is the skill
selfCheck: Can I explain Cursor to a friend in one sentence?
Do I know one personal task I want it to help with this week?

modules.title: Folders, Files & Opening a Project
modules.subtitle: Your Personal Ops home base

sections.heading: Why a home folder matters
sections.body: Cursor works best when you open a folder (Cursor calls this a project or workspace). Think of it as putting all the papers for a job onto one desk. Create a folder named something like Personal-Ops and keep your life-ops materials there.

sections.heading: Suggested starter tree
sections.body: Inbox/ (raw dumps), Projects/ (active efforts), Recipes/ (copy-paste prompts), Wins/ (prompts that worked), Reference/ (policies, bios, voice notes), Templates/ (email skeletons, meeting notes), Archive/. You can ask Cursor later to refine this — start simple.

sections.heading: How to open it
sections.body: In Cursor: File → Open Folder → select Personal-Ops. On the left you will see your files. That sidebar is your map. If you ever feel lost, click the top folder name and breathe — everything for this system lives here.

sections.heading: Text files are your friends
sections.body: Prefer .md (Markdown) or .txt for notes. They are simple, searchable, and AI-friendly. You can still keep PDFs and images nearby; Cursor can read many of them when you point to them.

keyTakeaways: Always Open Folder — don't work from random Desktop scraps alone
A simple tree beats a perfect tree you never use
Markdown notes are the sweet spot for beginners
selfCheck: Is Personal-Ops open in Cursor right now?
Can I find Inbox, Recipes, and Wins in the sidebar?

modules.title: Modes Without Jargon
modules.subtitle: Ask, Plan, Agent, Debug — when to use each

sections.heading: Ask = read-only brain
sections.body: Use Ask when you want answers, explanations, or options — and you do not want files changed yet. Example: 'Explain this PDF like I'm not technical' or 'What are 3 ways to organize my trip notes?'

sections.heading: Plan = architect before builders
sections.body: Use Plan for bigger or fuzzy jobs. Cursor researches, asks clarifying questions, and writes a step-by-step plan you can edit. You approve before building. Example: 'Plan a system to track home maintenance across seasons.'

sections.heading: Agent = do the work
sections.body: Use Agent when you are ready for Cursor to create/edit files, run careful computer steps, and iterate. You still review. Example: 'Create a weekly review template and a checklist for Monday mornings in Templates/.'

sections.heading: Debug = detective mode
sections.body: Use Debug when something is broken and guessing failed — especially for personal tools/scripts that misbehave. It gathers evidence instead of thrashing. Beginners use it less often, but knowing it exists reduces panic.

sections.heading: Your default path
sections.body: Unclear → Ask. Multi-step new system → Plan then Agent. Small known task → Agent. Weird breakage → Debug. When in doubt, start in Ask for 2 minutes, then switch.

keyTakeaways: Ask reads/explains; Plan designs; Agent executes; Debug investigates
selfCheck: Can I name all four modes and one example each?
Do I know my default path when unsure?

modules.title: How to Brief Cursor
modules.subtitle: Goal → Context → Constraints → Done-when

sections.heading: The four-part brief
sections.body: GOAL: what you want. CONTEXT: background + @files. CONSTRAINTS: what not to do (no deleting, keep my tone, under 200 words). DONE-WHEN: how you'll know it's finished (checklist, file created, questions answered). This beats 'help with email.'

sections.heading: Variables make briefs reusable
sections.body: Variables are fill-in-the-blank slots like {{GOAL}}, {{AUDIENCE}}, {{TONE}}, {{DEADLINE}}. Recipes in this course use them so you can copy a prompt and swap only the blanks. Treat Variables like Mad Libs for productivity.

sections.heading: Show, don't mystify
sections.body: Paste a sample of your voice. Point at a past email you liked. Attach a screenshot. Examples beat adjectives. 'Make it professional' is weak; 'Match the tone of @Reference/voice-samples.md' is strong.

sections.heading: One job per message (usually)
sections.body: Don't ask for a trip plan, tax folder cleanup, and a birthday speech in one blob. Split work. You can queue follow-ups while Agent runs, but each unit should be clear.

keyTakeaways: Variables turn one-off prompts into assets
selfCheck: Can I rewrite a vague ask into the four-part brief?
Do I have a Variables cheat sheet open?

modules.title: Stay in Control
modules.subtitle: Safety, review, undo, and private data

sections.heading: Never-paste list
sections.body: Do not paste passwords, one-time codes, full bank/card numbers, Social Security / national IDs, private medical details you wouldn't email, or API keys. If a tool needs a secret, use Cursor's proper Secrets / integration settings — not chat.

sections.heading: Review like a manager
sections.body: Read the diff summary (what changed). Skim created files. Check names and folders. If something feels off, Reject or restore a checkpoint. Checkpoints are local undo points for Agent changes — separate from long-term Git history.

sections.heading: Prefer copies before cleanup
sections.body: When organizing Downloads, ask Cursor to propose a plan and operate on a copy folder first (e.g., Downloads-Sort-Sandbox). Deleting comes last, manually, after you are happy.

sections.heading: Truth hygiene
sections.body: AI can sound confident and still be wrong. For facts that matter (health, legal, money, live prices, dates), require sources and verify. Your Recipe constraints should say 'Do not invent facts; mark unknowns.'

keyTakeaways: Review before Accept; use checkpoints to undo
selfCheck: Is my Never-Paste list written down?
Do I know how to reject a bad change?

modules.title: Giving Context with @
modules.subtitle: Pointing beats dumping your whole life story

sections.heading: Why @ exists
sections.body: Typing @ opens a menu to attach files, folders, docs, web, past chats, and more. It is how you put the right papers on the assistant's desk without rewriting everything.

sections.heading: Let Agent search when you don't know the file
sections.body: If you know the file, @ it. If you don't, describe it — Agent can search. Don't attach ten irrelevant files 'just in case'; that confuses the helper.

sections.heading: Screenshots and images
sections.body: Paste a screenshot of an error, a confusing website, or a flyer. Add one sentence: what you want done with it. Visual context is often faster than describing pixels.

sections.heading: @Past Chats
sections.body: Starting fresh? Reference a past chat instead of copy-pasting a novel. Fresh chats help when topics change; continuity helps when iterating the same job.

keyTakeaways: Fewer relevant files beat many random ones
selfCheck: Can I attach a file with @ without panic?
Do I know when to start a new chat?

modules.title: Your First Real Win
modules.subtitle: Week 1 capstone — one chore done end-to-end

sections.heading: Pick a win-sized chore
sections.body: Good size: rewrite a messy email; turn meeting notes into actions; draft a weekend itinerary from bullet chaos; create a template you'll reuse. Bad size: 'organize my entire digital life.'

sections.heading: Run the path
sections.body: Ask (clarify) → optional Plan → Agent (produce files) → Review → Save prompt to Wins/. Write one sentence: what Variable made the biggest difference?

sections.heading: Celebrate boring excellence
sections.body: Daily drivers are built on boring wins repeated. Screenshot the result into Wins/ if it helps motivation. Then stop — don't immediately stack five more chores tonight.

keyTakeaways: Ship one real win, not ten half-wins
Save the prompt — that's the asset
selfCheck: Is there a file in Wins/ from today?
Could I rerun this next week in 2 minutes?

modules.title: User Rules = Standing Orders
modules.subtitle: Teach Cursor your preferences once

sections.heading: What User Rules are
sections.body: User Rules are global instructions Cursor sees often — like standing orders for every job. Examples: 'Explain jargon in parentheses', 'Prefer bullet lists', 'Ask before deleting files', 'Default tone: warm, direct, no hype'.

sections.heading: Keep them short
sections.body: Rules consume attention. Start with 5–10 lines. Add a rule only when you correct the same mistake twice. Official guidance: don't paste entire style guides — point to examples instead.

sections.heading: Where to set them
sections.body: In Cursor: Customize → Rules (User Rules). Also explore /create-rule in Agent when you want help drafting. Official docs: https://cursor.com/docs/rules

selfCheck: Do I have User Rules saved?
Did I test one writing task against them?

modules.title: Project Memory
modules.subtitle: AGENTS.md and project rules for Personal Ops

sections.heading: Project rules vs user rules
sections.body: User Rules follow you everywhere. Project rules live in this folder's .cursor/rules/ and apply to Personal Ops specifically — naming conventions, folder meanings, templates to prefer.

sections.heading: AGENTS.md — the simple version
sections.body: A markdown file at the project root that tells any agent how this workspace works. Great for laymen: write it like onboarding a smart intern. Include folder map, do/don't, and where Recipes live.

sections.heading: Rules vs Skills (preview)
sections.body: Rules are always-on. Skills are on-demand playbooks (like /weekly-review) loaded when relevant. Don't shove rare workflows into always-on rules.

keyTakeaways: Rare workflows → skills, not always-on rules
selfCheck: Does Personal Ops have an AGENTS.md?
Could a stranger help me using only that file?

modules.title: Writing & Document Workflows
modules.subtitle: Email, docs, agendas, and voice

sections.heading: The writing loop
sections.body: Dump bullets → ask for structure → choose a tone → generate draft → you edit the human parts (feelings, commitments, numbers) → save final + prompt to Wins/.

sections.heading: Voice file
sections.body: Keep Reference/voice-samples.md with 3 short paragraphs that sound like you. @ that file in every important writing Recipe. This single habit upgrades quality more than any fancy model tweak.

sections.heading: Document types you will reuse
sections.body: Email, apology/repair note, meeting agenda, decision one-pager, newsletter blurb, bio/about blurb, FAQ. Each gets a Recipe with Variables.

keyTakeaways: Bullets in → structured draft out → human edit
selfCheck: Do I have voice-samples.md?
Did I ship one real email via Recipe?

modules.title: Research & The Web
modules.subtitle: Find, compare, cite — don't invent

sections.heading: Research brief pattern
sections.body: State the question, audience, and decision it informs. Ask for options with pros/cons, unknowns, and sources. Require: 'Label confidence; do not invent citations.'

sections.heading: @Web and browsing
sections.body: Use web tools / @Web when freshness matters. For local decisions (your own notes), prefer @Folder. Cursor can also use browser tools in agent workflows to inspect pages — still verify critical facts.

sections.heading: From research to action
sections.body: End every research job with: Decision you need to make, Recommended next step, Open questions. Research without a decision hook becomes trivia.

keyTakeaways: Always end with what you must decide
selfCheck: Can I spot a hallucinated-sounding claim?
Did my last brief include sources + unknowns?

modules.title: Organize & Automate Files
modules.subtitle: Cleanup, naming, tables, light automation

sections.heading: Sandbox first
sections.body: Copy a slice of messy files into Inbox/sandbox-sort/. Ask Agent to propose a plan in a markdown file. Approve. Then execute. Only trash originals manually later.

sections.heading: Naming convention
sections.body: Example: YYYY-MM-DD_topic_slug.md — 2026-07-28_trip-portugal_itinerary.md. Put the convention in AGENTS.md so every future agent obeys it.

sections.heading: Tables & CSV
sections.body: Paste a messy list and ask for CSV with clear columns. Open in Sheets/Excel. This is how a non-tech user builds trackers without 'building an app' on day one.

keyTakeaways: CSV is a friendly automation stepping stone
selfCheck: Did I sandbox before sorting?
Is my naming rule written down?

modules.title: Life Ops Playbook
modules.subtitle: Trips, errands, admin, family logistics

sections.heading: Separate facts from preferences
sections.body: Facts: dates, budget ceiling, number of people. Preferences: walkable > driving, quiet hotels, allergy constraints. Put both in Variables so Recipes stay honest.

sections.heading: Checklists beat paragraphs
sections.body: For life ops, ask for checklists with owners and due dates. Paragraph travel essays are pretty; checklists get bags packed.

sections.heading: Human gates
sections.body: Mark steps that require you: book payment, call doctor, confirm with spouse. AI should never silently 'decide' those.

selfCheck: Does my trip Recipe include budget + human gates?
Would a partner understand the checklist?

modules.title: Assemble Your Ops Kit
modules.subtitle: Week 2 — turn wins into a kit

sections.heading: What belongs in the kit
sections.body: Recipes/, Variables cheat sheet, voice samples, templates, Never-Paste list, AGENTS.md, and a 'How I use Cursor' one-pager.

sections.heading: Quality bar
sections.body: Each Recipe must have: purpose, Variables, steps, done-when, safety note. If a prompt worked once but isn't documented, it doesn't count yet.

keyTakeaways: Quality bar beats pile of scraps
selfCheck: Do I have ≥8 documented Recipes?
Can I find the Variables cheat sheet in <10 seconds?

modules.title: Skills = Repeat Buttons
modules.subtitle: Slash workflows you run every week

sections.heading: Skills in plain English
sections.body: A Skill is a packaged playbook Cursor can load when relevant — or you can invoke on purpose (often via /name). Perfect for /weekly-review, /draft-email, /research-brief.

sections.heading: Rules vs Skills again
sections.body: Standing orders → Rules. Multi-step occasional/weekly playbooks → Skills. Official learn page: https://cursor.com/learn/customizing-agents

sections.heading: Design three personal skills
sections.body: /inbox-triage (sort notes into folders), /meeting-to-actions, /weekend-plan. Write them as SKILL.md-style steps even if you store them as Recipes first.

selfCheck: Have I drafted 3 skill specs?
Do I know which of my rules should actually be skills?

modules.title: MCP Without Fear
modules.subtitle: Plug Cursor into the apps you already use

sections.heading: MCP = power strip
sections.body: Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets Cursor talk to external tools — docs, issue trackers, browsers, databases, search, etc. You are giving the assistant approved tools, not random internet powers.

sections.heading: Start with high-value, low-risk
sections.body: Good early connections: documentation search, calendar/notes systems you already trust, GitHub if you use it, browser tools for reading pages. Delay anything that can send mail or spend money until review habits are strong.

sections.heading: Marketplace & docs
sections.body: Browse Cursor Marketplace integrations and read https://cursor.com/docs/mcp. For Cloud Agents, configure MCP in the dashboard so cloud runs can use the same tools.

selfCheck: Can I explain MCP to a friend with the power-strip metaphor?
Have I picked 2 candidate integrations?

modules.title: Cloud Agents for Busy Humans
modules.subtitle: Delegate and close the laptop

sections.heading: What Cloud Agents are
sections.body: Cloud Agents run on Cursor's computers in the cloud. They clone your project, work on a branch, and hand back results — even if your laptop sleeps. Start from cursor.com/agents, desktop Cloud option, or mobile.

sections.heading: When to use cloud vs local
sections.body: Local: interactive back-and-forth, quick edits, you're at the desk. Cloud: longer jobs, parallel chores, kick off from your phone, 'todo list' tasks like tidy docs or draft a research pack while you live life.

sections.heading: Write cloud-ready briefs
sections.body: Cloud agents can't read your mind or your desk sticky notes. Put constraints, paths, and done-when in the brief. Connect GitHub/GitLab/etc. first. Docs: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent

keyTakeaways: Great for async personal projects in a repo
selfCheck: Can I write a self-contained cloud brief?
Do I know where to review results?

modules.title: Eyes & Browser
modules.subtitle: Screenshots, images, and page checks

sections.heading: Screenshot briefing
sections.body: Paste image → one-sentence goal → constraints. Example: 'Here's my utility bill portal error — tell me what it wants in plain English; don't ask me to paste passwords.'

sections.heading: Browser-assisted agent work
sections.body: Agents can navigate pages, take screenshots, and verify UI in supported workflows. Useful for checking a personal site or confirming a form layout — still your login.

sections.heading: Image generation (optional)
sections.body: Cursor can generate images for mockups/assets when you explicitly want visuals. For life ops, screenshots of reality usually beat generated pictures.

keyTakeaways: Browser tools verify, they don't replace your judgment
Be explicit when you want images generated
selfCheck: Did I solve one issue with a screenshot brief?

modules.title: Make It a Habit
modules.subtitle: Morning, midday, shutdown rituals

sections.heading: Morning (15–25 min)
sections.body: Open Personal Ops → Ask: 'Based on @Projects and @Inbox, what are today's top 3?' → pick one Agent job → queue the rest as notes.

sections.heading: Midday bump (10 min)
sections.body: Unstick one chore with Ask or a Recipe. Don't open ten chats. Finish or park with a written next step.

sections.heading: Shutdown (10–15 min)
sections.body: Move finished items to Archive/Wins → capture new Recipes → write tomorrow's top 3 → close Cursor. The shutdown is what makes tomorrow's morning easy.

sections.heading: New chat hygiene
sections.body: New chat when the topic changes or the agent seems lost. Continue when iterating the same job. Use @Past Chats to bridge.

selfCheck: Did I run morning + shutdown once?
Do I know when to start a new chat?

modules.title: Level-Up Patterns
modules.subtitle: Plan Mode, Debug, parallel work, review

sections.heading: Plan Mode muscle
sections.body: Toggle Plan Mode (Shift+Tab in agent input per Cursor docs) for multi-step systems. Edit the plan markdown. Save plans to the workspace when useful. If build goes wrong, revert and refine the plan — often faster than patching chaos.

sections.heading: Review checklist
sections.body: 1) Did it meet Done-when? 2) Any invented facts? 3) Tone match? 4) Files in right folders? 5) Secrets exposed? 6) What Variable/rule should we update?

sections.heading: Best practices source
sections.body: Read Cursor's own guide: https://cursor.com/blog/agent-best-practices — planning, context, rules/skills, cloud delegation, and review culture.

selfCheck: Have I completed one Plan→Build cycle?
Is my review checklist in Reference/?

modules.title: Mastery & Maintenance
modules.subtitle: Cursor as your daily driver — forever loop

sections.heading: What 'expert' means here
sections.body: Not writing compilers. An expert: picks modes instinctively, briefs with Variables, runs Recipes, maintains rules/skills, uses cloud for async, reviews ruthlessly, and teaches a friend the system.

sections.heading: 30-day maintenance
sections.body: Weekly: prune Recipes, add one new win, delete one unused rule. Monthly: revisit MCP, re-read one official changelog/blog, practice one advanced pattern.

sections.heading: Personal OS README
sections.body: Write HOW_I_USE_CURSOR.md covering: folder map, rituals, top Recipes, rules summary, safety list, and links to official docs. That file is your graduation artifact.

selfCheck: Does HOW_I_USE_CURSOR.md exist?
Can I teach this in 10 minutes?

recipes.title: Explain This Like I'm Not Technical
recipes.whenToUse: Anything confusing: a letter, PDF, settings screen, error message.
recipes.doneWhen: You understand the thing well enough to act or decide to ignore it.
recipes.safetyNote: Remove account numbers from screenshots when possible.

recipes.title: Plan a Personal System
recipes.whenToUse: You want a repeatable system (not a one-off answer).
recipes.doneWhen: You have an approved plan document you actually like.
recipes.safetyNote: Do not let it build before you approve the plan.

recipes.title: Draft an Email in My Voice
recipes.whenToUse: Any email you dread writing.
recipes.doneWhen: You can paste into your mail app after one edit.
recipes.safetyNote: Never include passwords; double-check promised dates.

recipes.title: Meeting Notes → Action List
recipes.whenToUse: After calls, school meetings, contractor visits.
recipes.doneWhen: Every action has an owner or TBD, and nothing important from notes is missing.
recipes.safetyNote: Confirm money/legal commitments yourself.

recipes.title: Decision Research Brief
recipes.whenToUse: Choosing between options; learning enough to decide.
recipes.doneWhen: You can decide — or know exactly what fact you're missing.
recipes.safetyNote: Verify prices, laws, and medical claims independently.

recipes.title: Summarize Links Fairly
recipes.whenToUse: You have articles/URLs and need a fair digest.
recipes.doneWhen: You see agreements and disagreements clearly.
recipes.safetyNote: Don't skip reading the key primary source for high-stakes topics.

recipes.title: Sandbox File Cleanup
recipes.whenToUse: Messy Downloads / Desktop chaos.
recipes.doneWhen: Sandbox looks right; originals untouched until you manually finish.
recipes.safetyNote: Never allow unsupervised delete on originals.

recipes.title: Messy List → CSV Tracker
recipes.whenToUse: Trips, inventories, gift lists, home tasks.
recipes.doneWhen: CSV imports cleanly with headers you understand.
recipes.safetyNote: No sensitive IDs in trackers you might share.

recipes.title: Trip Planner Checklist
recipes.whenToUse: Weekends away, family trips, work+personal travel.
recipes.doneWhen: You have a checklist you can execute — bookings still on you.
recipes.safetyNote: AI must not auto-book or invent visa rules.

recipes.title: Weekly Admin Sweep
recipes.whenToUse: Sunday/Monday life admin.
recipes.doneWhen: You know the only seven things that matter this week.
recipes.safetyNote: Don't let AI guilt you into a 40-item list.

recipes.title: Decision One-Pager
recipes.whenToUse: Buy vs wait; hire vs DIY; school choice framing.
recipes.doneWhen: A partner could read it and discuss calmly.
recipes.safetyNote: Separate facts from preferences explicitly.

recipes.title: Rewrite Keeping My Voice
recipes.whenToUse: You have a draft that sounds like a robot.
recipes.doneWhen: It sounds like me, not a brochure.
recipes.safetyNote: Check that meaning didn't shift on commitments.

recipes.title: Compare Vendors / Services
recipes.whenToUse: Contractors, software, insurance shopping (high-level).
recipes.doneWhen: You have questions ready for humans/vendors.
recipes.safetyNote: Not financial/legal advice — verify quotes yourself.

recipes.title: Build a Reusable Template
recipes.whenToUse: Meeting notes, weekly review, packing lists.
recipes.doneWhen: Template is saved and you used it once successfully.
recipes.safetyNote: Keep secrets out of templates.

recipes.title: Inbox Folder Triage
recipes.whenToUse: When Inbox/ is a junk drawer.
recipes.prompt:
MODE: Plan then Agent
GOAL: Triage @Inbox into Projects/Reference/Archive suggestions
CONSTRAINTS: Propose moves in a plan file first; wait for approval; no deletes
FORMAT: Table of file → suggested destination → why
RISK_TOLERANCE: {{RISK_TOLERANCE}}
recipes.doneWhen: Inbox has a clear plan; you approved moves.
recipes.safetyNote: Approve before any bulk moves.

recipes.title: Cloud Agent Async Brief
recipes.whenToUse: Jobs to kick off from phone or while away.
recipes.doneWhen: You can review a branch/PR without re-explaining context.
recipes.safetyNote: Connect source control; no secrets in the brief.

recipes.title: Screenshot Help
recipes.whenToUse: Errors, confusing UI, flyers, school forms.
recipes.prompt:
MODE: Ask
GOAL: {{GOAL}}
I pasted a screenshot.
Explain what I'm looking at in plain English.
Tell me the safest next click/action.
CONSTRAINTS: {{CONSTRAINTS}}
Do not ask me to paste passwords.
recipes.doneWhen: You know what to click — or what to avoid.
recipes.safetyNote: Crop sensitive info from images.

recipes.title: Weekly Review Ritual
recipes.whenToUse: End of week reflection + next week setup.
recipes.prompt:
MODE: Agent
GOAL: Run weekly review using my folders
FILES: @Wins @Projects @Inbox
FORMAT:
1) Wins this week
2) Stuck / waiting-on
3) Lessons → new Recipe or Rule?
4) Next week Top 7
OUTPUT_PATH: Projects/weekly/{{DATES}}.md
TONE: Encouraging but honest
recipes.doneWhen: Next week's Top 7 exists and Inbox is lighter.
recipes.safetyNote: Don't turn review into self-attack.

recipes.title: Draft User Rules From Complaints
recipes.whenToUse: You keep correcting Cursor the same way.
recipes.prompt:
MODE: Ask then help me save rules
GOAL: Turn my recurring corrections into short User Rules
INPUT_DUMP:
{{INPUT_DUMP}}
CONSTRAINTS: Max 10 bullet rules; crisp; no essays
FORMAT: Paste-ready User Rules markdown
recipes.doneWhen: Rules are short and installed.
recipes.safetyNote: Don't encode rare one-offs as global rules.

recipes.title: Teach-Back Check
recipes.whenToUse: Before you trust you learned something.
recipes.prompt:
MODE: Ask
GOAL: Quiz me on {{GOAL}} like a patient coach
AUDIENCE: non-technical
FORMAT: 5 questions; wait for my answers; then grade kindly with corrections
SUCCESS_CRITERIA: I can teach this to a friend
recipes.doneWhen: You can explain it without reading notes.
recipes.safetyNote: None special.

recipes.title: Family Logistics Board
recipes.whenToUse: Multiple people, multiple calendars, chaos.
recipes.doneWhen: Everyone knows their next action.
recipes.safetyNote: Confirm with humans before treating TBD as real.

recipes.title: Turn How I Do It Into a Mini SOP
recipes.whenToUse: When only you know how a household/admin process works.
recipes.doneWhen: Someone else could follow the SOP cold.
recipes.safetyNote: Omit secrets; point to where secrets live.

recipes.title: Repurpose One Note Many Ways
recipes.whenToUse: Newsletter, social, email, FAQ from one brain dump.
recipes.doneWhen: Three usable variants without starting from blank.
recipes.safetyNote: Fact-check before publishing.

recipes.title: Debug a Personal Tool
recipes.whenToUse: A tracker/script/page you use personally is broken.
recipes.doneWhen: Issue fixed or you have a clear blocker.
recipes.safetyNote: Back up files before big changes.

glossary.definition: Mode where Cursor can edit files and take multi-step actions you review.
Mode for questions and explanations with minimal/no editing focus.
Mode that researches and drafts an editable plan before building.
Mode for evidence-based diagnosis of stubborn problems.
Your global standing instructions to Cursor.
Instructions stored in a project (often `.cursor/rules`).
Simple root markdown file that onboard agents to a workspace.
On-demand playbook/workflow Cursor can load or you invoke (e.g. /name).
Model Context Protocol — a standard way to connect external tools.
Agent running on a Cursor cloud VM, usable async/mobile/web.
Local restore point for Agent file changes.
Copy-paste prompt template with Variables for a recurring job.
Placeholder like {{GOAL}} you fill each time you run a Recipe.
The folder you opened in Cursor — the assistant's desk.
Plain text with light formatting; ideal for notes and Recipes.
A view of what changed in files — read before accepting.
Information the model can use (files, chat, web, images).
Confident-sounding invented fact — verify important claims.
A step only you should perform (pay, send, legal commit).
Copy of files used for safe cleanup experiments.
Your documented set of Recipes, rules, templates, and safety lists.
The default tool you reach for most days for this class of work.
Clear instructions: goal, context, constraints, done-when.
Observable definition of finished.
Typing @ to attach specific context objects.
Cursor place to discover integrations/extensions.
Screenshot/video/log evidence produced by agents (esp. cloud).
A proposed set of changes for review in GitHub/GitLab etc.
Version history system; useful backups beyond checkpoints.
Searchable command launcher (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P).
Inline suggestions you accept with Tab while typing.
The AI brain choice powering a chat/agent run.
Rough measure of how much text/compute a plan meters.
Standard Operating Procedure — documented repeatable process.
Short writing examples that sound like you.
Library of prompts/outputs that worked.
Raw unsorted dumps awaiting triage.
Hard limits in a brief (don't delete; don't invent).
Repeatable QA list before you trust AI output.
Multiple agents working separately to compare results.
Isolated working copy so parallel agents don't collide.
Scripts that run around agent actions (advanced automation).
Helper agent spun up for a focused subtask.
Preconfigured cloud machine setup (tools, deps, secrets).
Sensitive values stored in secure settings — not in chat.
Official list of product changes — skim monthly.
Learning check where you explain a topic in your own words.
your life/work operations system inside a Cursor folder.
Travel, errands, family logistics, household admin.
Simple table file Sheets/Excel can open.
Single-page decision or summary document.
Follow-up instructions waiting while Agent finishes current work.
Keep or discard proposed AI edits.
Your personal ban list of secrets not to put in chat.

cheatSheets.title: Mode picker (print me)
cheatSheets.body:
ASK — explain, compare, brainstorm (don't change files yet)
PLAN — fuzzy/multi-step systems; approve plan first
AGENT — do the work with review
DEBUG — broken thing; need evidence

Default: Unclear→Ask → (Plan?) → Agent → Review

cheatSheets.title: Four-part brief
cheatSheets.body:
GOAL:
CONTEXT:
CONSTRAINTS:
DONE-WHEN / SUCCESS_CRITERIA:

Optional: AUDIENCE, TONE, LENGTH, FORMAT, FILES (@...), EXAMPLES, REVIEW_GATE

cheatSheets.title: Never-Paste
cheatSheets.body:
Passwords & OTP codes
Full card/bank numbers
Government IDs
API keys/tokens
Private data you wouldn't email casually

Use Secrets/settings/integrations instead.

cheatSheets.title: Daily ritual
cheatSheets.body:
MORNING: Open Personal Ops → Top 3 → one Agent job
MIDDAY: Unstick one chore with a Recipe
SHUTDOWN: Wins/Archive → capture Recipe → tomorrow Top 3 → close

cheatSheets.title: Review checklist
cheatSheets.body:
1 Done-when met?
2 Any invented facts?
3 Tone/voice OK?
4 Files in right places?
5 Secrets exposed?
6 Update a Rule/Recipe?
7 Human gates still on me?

cheatSheets.title: Personal Ops folder map
cheatSheets.body:
Inbox/ raw
Projects/ active
Recipes/ prompts
Wins/ keepers
Reference/ voice, SOPs, never-paste
Templates/ skeletons
Archive/ done

trainerPrompts.prompt: Which mode first? I don't understand this insurance letter.
Which mode first? Build me a reusable weekly review template set in my folder.
trainerPrompts.explain: Clear build → Agent (or Plan if fuzzy).

trainerPrompts.prompt: Which mode first? I want a system for tracking home repairs across seasons — not sure structure.
Which mode first? My personal checklist webpage shows blank after yesterday's edit.
Which mode first? Brainstorm 10 names for a family reunion weekend.
Which mode first? Sort a copied sandbox of Downloads using our naming rules.
Which mode first? Design how Recipes/, Wins/, and Templates/ should interact — then we'll build.
Which mode first? Why did Cursor change files I didn't expect? Explain the diff.
Which mode first? Create CSV from my pasted inventory notes after I confirm columns.
Which mode first? This automation script fails only sometimes when renaming files.
Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Draft an email.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Email drafts need audience/tone/goal at minimum. Also acceptable: AUDIENCE, TONE, GOAL.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Clean my files.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Cleanup needs scope + safety constraints. Also acceptable: RISK_TOLERANCE, FILES, CONSTRAINTS.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Research somehow.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Research needs question + done-when + no-invention policy. Also acceptable: GOAL, SUCCESS_CRITERIA, UNKNOWN_POLICY.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Make a trip plan.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Trips need when/who/money. Also acceptable: DATES, PEOPLE, BUDGET.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Write a one-pager.'
trainerPrompts.explain: One-pagers need reader + shape + background. Also acceptable: AUDIENCE, FORMAT, CONTEXT.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Run this in cloud.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Cloud needs self-contained done-when/path/limits. Also acceptable: SUCCESS_CRITERIA, OUTPUT_PATH, CONSTRAINTS.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Rewrite this to sound like me.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Voice needs samples + input. Also acceptable: EXAMPLES, TONE, INPUT_DUMP.

trainerPrompts.prompt: Name one critical missing Variable category: 'Compare two vendors.'
trainerPrompts.explain: Comparisons need criteria and ceiling. Also acceptable: GOAL, BUDGET, PRIORITY.

Which mode first? Explain Plan vs Agent like I'm not technical.
Which mode first? Implement the approved plan in Personal Ops.
Which mode first? Propose folder conventions for family logistics.
Which mode first? Quiz me on Never-Paste.
Which mode first? Generate a packing checklist file.
Which mode first? Something regresses every time I add a new section to my notes site.
Which mode first? What should be a Rule vs a Skill here?
Which mode first? Kick off an async tidy job brief suitable for cloud.
Which mode first? Apply naming convention across sandbox files.
Which mode first? The CSV opens with broken columns.
Which mode first? Help me pick Top 7 from a messy list.
Which mode first? Create HOW_I_USE_CURSOR.md from my notes.
Which mode first? Map a 30-day maintenance cadence before writing it.
Which mode first? Screenshot of portal error — what does it want?
Which mode first? Build decision one-pager from my bullets.
Which mode first? Approach for connecting MCP without wrecking safety.

mnemonics.title: GCCD
mnemonics.body: Goal → Context → Constraints → Done-when. Every brief.

mnemonics.title: APAD
mnemonics.body: Ask · Plan · Agent · Debug — four gears.

mnemonics.title: Boss not spectator
mnemonics.body: Brief clearly, review diffs, own human gates.

mnemonics.title: Sandbox before shredder
mnemonics.body: Copy → plan → approve → execute → manual trash later.

mnemonics.title: Rules lean, Skills on demand
mnemonics.body: Standing orders short; playbooks as skills/recipes.

mnemonics.title: Wins are assets
mnemonics.body: Save the prompt that worked — future-you is the customer.

dailyDriverOS.name: Cursor Personal OS
coreRules: Explain jargon in plain English parentheses
Ask before deleting or moving originals
Do not invent facts; mark unknowns
Prefer Markdown in Templates/ and Projects/
Default tone: warm, direct, no hype
Always include DONE-WHEN in your replies when producing deliverables

weekly: Delete or shorten one unused rule
